record.paper_title: Conjectures and Open Questions on the Structure and Regularity of Spaces with Lower Ricci Curvature Bounds
record.original_question: Suppose a sequence of pointed n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds (M_i^n, g_i, p_i) converges in the Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space (X, d, p), with Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0. For a fixed point x in X, are all tangent cones at x homeomorphic to one another outside a subset of codimension five?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.9. Let Mni, gi, pi → (X, d, p) satisfy Ric ≥ −(n − 1) and Vol(B1(pi)) > v > 0, then the tangent cones of X are all homoemorphic at a fixed point away from a set of codimension five.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ be a sequence of pointed complete $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds satisfying the uniform lower Ricci curvature bound $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} \ge -(n-1)$ and the noncollapsing condition $\mathrm{Vol}(B_1(p_i)) > v > 0$ for some fixed $v>0$. Assume that $(M_i^n, g_i, p_i)$ converges in the pointed Gromov–Hausdorff sense to a metric space $(X, d, p)$.

Recall that a tangent cone of $X$ at a point $x \in X$ is any pointed Gromov–Hausdorff limit of a rescaled sequence $(X, r_j^{-1} d, x)$ with $r_j \to 0$; in the noncollapsed setting above, every such sequence has subsequential limits, but the limit need not be unique.

Prove or disprove: for every fixed point $x \in X$, there exists a closed subset $S_x \subset X$ of Hausdorff codimension at least five such that, for any two tangent cones $C_1$ and $C_2$ of $X$ at $x$, the complements $C_1 \setminus \widetilde{S}_x$ and $C_2 \setminus \widetilde{S}_x$ are homeomorphic, where $\widetilde{S}_x$ denotes the corresponding subsets in the tangent cones. Equivalently, all tangent cones of $X$ at $x$ are homeomorphic away from a set of codimension five.
artifact.category_tag: Ricci limit spaces and tangent cones
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears still open in general dimensions. Colding–Naber constructed examples in dimension 5 showing tangent cones at a point need not be homeomorphic, motivating the codimension-five formulation. Recent work (e.g., Wang 2024, arXiv:2405.03839) confirms a related Colding–Naber conjecture in dimension 4 (cross-sections of tangent cones are spherical space forms), and Naber's k-symmetry conjecture is connected, but no source verifies the full codimension-five homeomorphism statement for general n.

status_evidence.title: Topological regularity and stability of noncollapsed spaces with Ricci curvature bounded below
status_evidence.snippet: confirm a conjecture proposed by Colding and Naber in dimension n=4, showing that the cross-sections of tangent cones at a given point are all homeomorphic to a fixed spherical space form S^3/Γ_x
status_evidence.claim: A related Colding–Naber conjecture has been resolved only in dimension 4, not in general.

status_evidence.title: Examples of tangent cones of non-collapsed Ricci limit spaces
status_evidence.snippet: in dimension 5, two different homeomorphism types appear at the same point; limit spaces in all dimensions at least 5 can be constructed where any finite collection of manifolds appear as cross sections of tangent cones at the same point
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness of homeomorphism type of tangent cones is known starting in dimension 5, consistent with codimension five being the predicted threshold; the conjecture remains unresolved.
